clue.text: Estimation of the age of an item?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: working out how old something is
second meaning: a couple who are an item are going out together, courting

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about valuing an antique; split it, and 'item' turns from an object into a romantic couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both establishing a period for an artefact and the courtship state of a pair seeing each other.

clue.text: This great tree grows from an outside well!

indicators.note: the two letters of an sit outside, wrapping the next word

parts.note: cor and well are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A tree growing up from beside a well.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says great oaks from little ones grow; the exclamation mark marks the 'well' as an interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak, a great tree, sprouts from its seed, the small nut in a cup.

clue.text: Together plotting reaction to superb "old people" gag?

parts.note: the Inca were an ancient South American people
hoots of laughter are the reaction to a superb joke, the gag of the clue

explanation.surface: Conspirators react to a great joke about elderly folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the answer is what an Inca joke earns: the 'old people' are the Inca, not pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is an idiom for being in secret partnership or collusion with someone.

clue.text: Bright guy with books on Zoology's heading for University

indicators.note: the new letters stand in for, replacing, the university letter

parts.note: taken as written
lit, short for literature, means books

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is wanted

explanation.surface: A clever chap who reads up on zoology on his way to university.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitzy means showily glamorous and sparkling, so it can stand for bright in the flashy sense.

clue.text: Her words ill-chosen, as for representative cases

indicators.note: the MP encases the other letters, holding them between its two letters

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
the French phrase à la means in the manner of, as
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A comment on someone whose speech is full of badly picked words, offered with a lawyerly 'as for representative cases'.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Malaprop is the character in Sheridan's play The Rivals who keeps using the wrong, similar-sounding word; 'her' points to that woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Malaprop, Sheridan's comic character, gave her name to the malapropism because her vocabulary was so often misapplied.

clue.text: After rebuilding, asks farm and theatre to do it?

definitions.text: After rebuilding, asks farm and theatre to do it?

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are reconstructed into a new order

explanation.surface: After a refurbishment, a farm and a theatre are both asked to begin again.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ASKS FARM THEATRE is itself what rebuilding asks of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a fresh start is an idiom for beginning anew, which is what a rebuilt enterprise does.

clue.text: Learned of healthy eating speed?

parts.note: lite is the label on low-calorie diet foods
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A question about how fast a healthy diet works.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned here is the adjective: someone well read and educated, able to read and write well.

clue.text: Worn down? Contrariwise!

indicators.note: the other way round: the phrase for down is read from its end

parts.note: something down is not up

explanation.surface: Asking whether clothing is worn down, then answering the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like part of 'worn down', but it is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that have been put on are being worn, a phrasal-verb equivalent.

clue.text: Dismissed team has batting order reversed?

parts.note: a batsman dismissed is out
a side is a team
in cricket the batting side is in

explanation.surface: A cricket team, all out, finds its batting order turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside in describes something turned with its usual arrangement flipped, the opposite of inside out.

clue.text: Unfair verdict: grasshopper or locust, maybe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not sporting, against the spirit of fair play
second meaning: judging such an insect, one would say it is not a cricket, a related but different insect

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally as an entomologist's ruling: a grasshopper or locust is close kin to the cricket but is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something 'not cricket' is an idiom for behaviour that breaches fair play, taken from the gentlemanly ideals of that sport.

clue.text: Hats off to all Turners exhibited here

definitions.text: Hats off to all Turners exhibited here

indicators.note: the hats are the tops of the words, so only each word's opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A salute to a gallery that shows every painting by J.M.W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hats off' looks like a tribute, but it picks the heads of the next four words. The whole clue also describes the gallery: the Tate in London holds the Turner Bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tate Britain in London houses the huge Turner Bequest, so the gallery is where his paintings hang.

clue.text: Anorak oddly nailing theoretical position of Australia's coral?

indicators.note: the odd letters pin down and hold the next pieces between them
take the first, third and fifth letters of the word

parts.note: nth is the mathematician's arbitrary place in a series
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A nerdish anorak pins down where some Australian coral theoretically sits.
explanation.walkthrough: An anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, here simply a word to strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthozoa is the zoological class containing corals and sea anemones, so the term names the coral group.

clue.text: Picture-maker concerned with darker films?

parts.note: re means about, concerning
film noir is the shadowy crime-film genre

explanation.surface: An artist whose work deals with gloomy cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter, and pictures are what a painter produces.

clue.text: River taken to heart by the real Acton Bell!

indicators.note: only the centre of the name is kept, its outer letters shed

parts.note: Acton Bell was the pen name of Anne Brontë

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some river was dear to a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; Acton was Anne. Her full name has ten letters and the middle four are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river of north-east Spain, flowing to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Summarily flaunting bum in rave

indicators.note: showing off, these letters are paraded in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone at a rave abruptly shows off their bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Brevi manu is Latin for 'with a short hand', meaning promptly, without formality.

clue.text: Rigging where service personnel go to change sides?

indicators.note: left and right swap places, so the L and the R exchange positions

parts.note: latrines are military toilets

explanation.surface: A question about rigging on a ship, as if it were a route for defectors.
explanation.walkthrough: The L (left) and R (right) in the toilets word swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small ropes tied across a sailing ship's shrouds, forming ladders in the rigging.

clue.text: Private nurses look up local manager

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the outer word holds the next piece

parts.note: inner means private, personal

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: peek means a quick look

explanation.surface: A soldier caring for someone looks up the pub manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier, but it means inner. A local is a British neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a neighbourhood pub, and an innkeeper runs a pub or inn.

clue.text: Lost lads say, over my dead body, "Go back to the sign"

indicators.note: lost lads are scattered, so their letters wander into a new order

parts.note: eg is short for for example, say
an emphatic refusal: no

explanation.surface: Lost boys are told, emphatically, to go back to the signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: Dal segno is the musical instruction telling a player to repeat from the sign marked in the score.

clue.text: Gatecrashers at Oscars after-party will no doubt be dazed

definitions.text: Gatecrashers at Oscars after-party will no doubt
definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally catch sight of celebrities
second meaning: to be stunned, as after a blow on the head

explanation.walkthrough: The literal sense is spotting film celebrities; the idiom is the blurred vision after a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow to the head makes one see stars, an idiom for being stunned or dizzy.

clue.text: This is impossible without oxygen

parts.note: non is Latin and French for not, here read as without
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A note that something cannot happen when there is no oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-no is something forbidden or not possible, an informal term for what simply cannot be done.

clue.text: Passing over sweet cryptically represented by end columns

parts.note: handing means passing over to someone
love, like sweet, is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: Handing over a sweet, as shown by the end columns.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid's outer columns hide UP CLOSE AND (read upwards) and PERSONAL, a phrase the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Working hand in glove means being in very close and intimate partnership, matching up close and personal.

clue.text: Harnessing one Russian woman's fuel

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the numeral within it

parts.note: Olga is a typical Russian woman's name, with its possessive S
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Russian woman's fuel supply, with one harnessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil-gas is a fuel gas made by heating petroleum oil, used for lighting and heating.

clue.text: See 20
NIRDLA ZZUB?

parts.note: the clue is a famous name in capitals written backwards; written backwards in turn, the answer reads NAME CAPS, describing it, and the man named is an astronaut

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is BUZZ ALDRIN written backwards and in capitals: a reversed 'name caps'. Reversed, that gives the answer, and Aldrin, the second man on the Moon, is a spaceman too.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz Aldrin, the Apollo 11 astronaut, is the spaceman whose name the clue shows reversed.

clue.text: A frameless doorway through which vital commodity is transported

definitions.text: through which vital commodity is transported

indicators.note: the word loses its outside letters, its frame

parts.note: a portal is a doorway

explanation.surface: A doorway without a frame used for shifting important goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying oxygenated blood from the heart, so blood passes through it.

clue.text: French scorer's wind-down, perhaps, after sapping S&M?

indicators.note: once the S and M are drained away, what is left is the answer

parts.note: a slalom is a winding run down a ski slope

explanation.surface: A French composer's way of relaxing, once kinky activity has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: S&M names the two letters taken off the ends of the ski race.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Lalo was a French composer, and a scorer is one who writes musical scores.

clue.text: For one Guillaume Tell artist, good printed info may be read in advance

indicators.note: the good printed info is read ahead of the artist, so those pieces come first

parts.note: a newspaper ran a story when it printed it
dope is slang for information
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's advance notes on William Tell, with good printed information to read beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: Although the artist is named first, 'may be read in advance' sends G, RAN and DOPE ahead of RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's Guillaume Tell is a classic example of the large-scale French operatic genre with chorus and ballet.

clue.text: One is one's own man, no longer leading Englishmen behind block

indicators.note: the cricketer comes after the block in the answer

parts.note: a cube is a solid block
Joe Root had just stepped down as England's Test cricket captain

explanation.surface: A man stepping back from leading the English, his independence asserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root resigned as England Test captain in April 2022, weeks before this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Since one times one times one is one, the number whose cube equals one is one itself.

clue.text: Know army pals uncovered standard

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, its covers removed

explanation.surface: Knowing your army friends with nothing hidden is the usual thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and standard are synonyms meaning usual or conforming to the expected type.
